**Marketing Intern · 3 days per week (9 am–5 pm)**

Join the Yogurberry Australia Head Office marketing team and help keep our day-to-day marketing running smoothly. You’ll coordinate campaigns with franchise partners, respond to customer enquiries and keep marketing records up to date. You’ll also create content for our social channels and campaigns.

This is a **12-month internship with the opportunity to move into a permanent role based on performance**.

**What you’ll do**

* Liaise with franchise partners to share campaign updates, coordinate in-store promotions and follow up on action items.
* Respond to customer enquiries professionally and refer issues to the relevant team when needed.
* Maintain campaign calendars, spreadsheets and marketing files.
* Help prepare campaign materials, schedule social media posts and support store openings and brand activations.
* Shoot and edit product photos and short-form videos, including occasional shoots at Yogurberry stores.

**What we’re looking for**

* **Previous administration experience**, with the ability to organise tasks, maintain accurate records and follow up reliably.
* **Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace**, including Word, Excel, Outlook, Google Docs, Sheets and Drive.
* **Practical photography and videography skills**, including the ability to shoot and edit your own work.
* Ability to create marketing assets using **Canva, Adobe Creative Cloud**
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence dealing with franchise partners and customers.
* Availability to work on-site at our Silverwater Head Office three days per week, from 9 am to 5 pm.

University students and recent graduates are welcome to apply. Administration experience can come from paid work, volunteering or a student society. Personal and university projects are welcome in your portfolio.

**How to apply**

Apply on Indeed via this website and include the following with your application.

* **Your résumé**, highlighting any administration, customer service or marketing experience.
* **A portfolio or link to your work** with examples of your photography, videography and graphic design. Include design samples that show what you can create using Canva, Adobe Creative Cloud or another design program. For each design sample, name the software you used and briefly describe your contribution.
* **Your availability**, including which weekdays you can work on-site at our Silverwater Head Office from 9 am to 5 pm.

University assignments, personal projects and work samples are welcome. If you’re sharing a portfolio link, please check that we can open it without requesting access.

**About Anthropic**

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

We are seeking a Partner Marketing Lead, APAC, reporting to the Global Head of Partner Marketing, to own partner marketing end to end across a region where partners are central to how Claude reaches enterprises. As our founding APAC Partner Marketing leader, you'll set the plan for the region rather than execute one set elsewhere: you'll build the operating model, carry partner pipeline goals, and turn our work with hyperscale cloud providers, global and regional systems integrators, resellers, and technology partners into a regional go-to-market motion that creates pipeline and drives adoption of Claude.

The central challenge is sequencing: ANZ, ASEAN, India, Japan, and Korea differ in their partner ecosystems, buyers, languages, and maturity. In some, local partners are the main route to enterprise customers, and India's systems integrators also deliver for customers worldwide. You'll decide where to invest first, where a global or partner-led program is enough for now, and where to wait.

This role calls for the seniority to lead a regional organization and the willingness to start hands-on with a very small team, defining the regional team plan and then hiring and managing the team as headcount opens. The role covers the whole region, including Japan, where you'll build on an established Partner Marketing presence, so that partners and sales teams experience one connected regional approach.

* Define the regional team plan and make the case for where to add capacity

The TD will participate in the development of artist workflows and tools for projects and debug problematic workflow steps to support global studio productions in that area. The TD will work closely with their craft groups and show leadership, the Solutions Engineering and R&D teams to enable high-quality technical outcomes and a standardized approach.

  
  

**What You’ll Do:**

  

* Provide technical expertise and guidance for Houdini and USD technology for the departments they support.
* Understand the visual requirements for productions and propose new technologies, or design procedures, techniques, and tools to ensure those needs are met.
* Provide technical expertise and guidance for technology within the PAFX department.
* Participate in or lead the direction, evolution & maintenance of technology within the PAFX department.
* Design, develop, review and write well-maintainable, production level and consistently high-quality code.
* Track, debug, and resolve workflow issues in partnership with technical supervisors, associate technical supervisors, solutions engineers, and R&D.
* Work closely with other TD’s on the team to drive the technical success of key development initiatives.
* Communicate clearly, via instant messaging systems like Slack, to proactively report on issues that may affect others, provide updates on software releases, and offer assistance to other team members.
* Ensure that technology, tools, and procedures support the creative process.
* Provide solutions to visual problems through existing tools or by leading the implementation of new tools.
* Take responsibility for the troubleshooting & optimization of the tools, software, and workflows of the PAFX department.
* Actively participate in or drive QA, technical testing, and validation of new technology, tool releases, or pipeline changes such that artist workflow is not impacted.
* Understand the processes of adjoining departments and provide input where required to maximize pipeline efficiency and quality.
* Actively participate in brainstorming and problem-solving, contributing technical expertise and insight, to create and maintain technology within the canonical production pipeline.

* Demonstrate excellent communication skills, including the ability to clearly present work to stakeholders, actively gather feedback, and incorporate it into technical solutions.
* Be aware of the deadlines for development initiatives and actively engage in keeping these on track.
* Continuously monitor the scope of development initiatives and help to ensure scope adjustments have additional estimates, etc.
* Prioritize and break down technical projects into organized parts and describe them in Jira
* Provide technical guidance to other TDs and TAs, where appropriate, with day-to-day issues and escalation through the right channels when necessary.
* Mentor junior team members and assist in orientation with new starters.
* Create synergies between different work groups to promote efficiency and optimization and to generate innovative ideas and approaches to how we do things
  

  

**What You’ll Need:**

  

Experience:

* 5+ years of proven pipeline TD experience in large-scale animated features, animated TV series, the gaming industry, and/or VFX feature films.
* Solid production/industry experience as a TD, ideally as part of a team.

* Comprehensive Houdini experience with using and troubleshooting procedural node-based workflows.

* An understanding of traditional techniques appropriate to Assets (Surfacing, hair and feather grooming, lookdev, procedural vegetation, or environment modelling)

**About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.  
  
If you would like to feel a strong connection to your work and you are accountable, committed and open to change, join us in shaping Australia’s future.  
  
Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

**The National Measurement Institute**  
  
We are the Australian Government’s national authority on measurement.  
  
At the National Measurement Institute (NMI), we empower innovation and protect trust in Australian industry and society through world-class measurement science. Join a team where your expertise drives national impact, your curiosity is nurtured, and the work you do creates trusted measurement for a fair, safe, healthy, and competitive Australia. Our employees enjoy career development opportunities, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to shape Australia’s economic future through world-class measurement science.  
  
At NMI, precision meets purpose.  
  
We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and impactful workplace by hiring people who share our values and bring integrity, collaboration, and innovation to everything they do.  
  
**Physical Metrology Branch**  
  
NMI’s Physical Metrology Branch provides Australia’s peak measurement standards for physical quantities. This enables measurements made in Australia to be accepted internationally, which is particularly important for trade. Our people share their expertise by providing measurement services from calibration and testing to technical advice and training. We contribute actively to international measurement forums and enhance our capabilities through research and development in line with national and international requirements.  
  
**Power Systems Technology Team**  
  
NMI's Power Systems Technology team develops advanced measurement technologies and delivers specialist testing and calibration services that support Australia's electricity network and clean energy transition. The team operates Australia's largest high-voltage and high-current laboratory and provides critical services to electric power utilities, equipment manufacturers and industry stakeholders. Supporting Australia's Net Zero ambitions, our work underpins the generation, storage, transmission and use of clean energy. Its capabilities span three key areas: high-voltage testing and calibration, calibration of power system voltage and current sensors, and the design and manufacture of highly accurate digital and analogue measurement systems.  
  
The team delivers more than 30 specialised testing and calibration services across a diverse range of power system equipment and measurement parameters. It also undertakes applied research in collaboration with universities, national metrology institutes and industry partners to develop innovative measurement techniques and technologies. Our team's experts contribute to the development of Australian and international standards through active participation in Standards Australia and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). We provide technical leadership across a range of national and international working groups, helping shape the future of power system measurement science and engineering.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

This is a senior opportunity for an experienced electrical or power system engineer to apply their expertise to nationally significant infrastructure and measurement challenges. The role supports Australia’s high-voltage and high-current measurement capability, helping ensure that critical electricity infrastructure can be tested, calibrated and assessed with confidence.  
  
The Senior Electrical Scientist/Metrologist will work at the interface of practical power engineering, specialised measurement systems and national standards. The role involves leading or contributing to high-value testing and calibration services, capability development, applied research, stakeholder engagement, and representation in national and international technical forums.  
  
As the electricity sector evolves—with increasing renewable generation, high-voltage transmission, power electronics, grid-scale storage and emerging electrical infrastructure—the role offers the opportunity to shape measurement capability that is directly relevant to industry, regulators and the national electricity system.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions, and support innovation in areas that include nanometrology, sports integrity, forensic analysis, cancer diagnostics, high voltage electricity, and clean energy. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
You will build sought-after experience leading nationally significant high-voltage testing, calibration and capability development, while deepening your expertise in measurement science and national standards.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave
* a vacation care subsidy
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy
* access to study assistance
* access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed.

For candidates with highly specialised skills and experience, remuneration above the standard salary may be considered through an Individual Flexibility Arrangement (IFA), subject to delegate approval and departmental policy.

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

* Leadership skills in a technical or scientific environment.
* Experience developing, operating or maintaining complex measurement, testing or calibration systems involving high-voltage and high-current applications.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving and innovation skills, including the ability to develop new measurement capabilities and improve existing test and calibration services.
* Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with clients, regulators, standards bodies, industry stakeholders and scientific peers.
* Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical information to a range of audiences and contribute to scientific publications, technical committees and professional forums.
* Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices, quality assurance and continuous improvement.

Additional qualities sought at the S&T8 level include:  

* Demonstrated leadership of scientific or technical teams, including mentoring and capability building.
* Experience developing strategic capability roadmaps, investment priorities and long-term technical programs.
* Demonstrated leadership and influence in technical forums related to national and international standards, accreditation or research.
* Recognition as a technical authority within a specialised field of measurement science or engineering.

**Qualifications**  

* Tertiary qualifications in Electrical Engineering, Physics or a closely related discipline.
* A postgraduate qualification or PhD in a relevant field would be highly regarded but is not essential.

*We’re looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI values (Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential, and Strategic) while upholding the APS Code of Conduct. Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way. Even if you’re not sure you meet all the requirements, we’d love to hear from you!*

**What you will do**
--------------------

* Lead or contribute to the development, maintenance and improvement of Australia's national high-voltage and high-current measurement standards, reference systems, traceability chains, uncertainty analyses and specialist capabilities.
* Deliver and oversee complex testing, calibration and measurement services, applying expert technical knowledge to solve complex measurement challenges and provide authoritative advice to clients and stakeholders.
* Drive innovation, research and service development activities to address emerging measurement needs and support future capability requirements within Australia's electricity sector.
* Lead or contribute to strategic capability, workforce and infrastructure planning, while providing technical leadership, supervision and mentoring to scientific and technical staff.
* Ensure laboratory operations comply with ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation requirements, NMI quality systems, technical procedures and workplace health and safety obligations.
* Build and maintain productive stakeholder relationships and represent NMI and Australia in national and international technical committees, standards development activities, accreditation forums, conferences and industry events.

**Classification Expectations**  
  
*S&T7*  
  
At the S&T7 level, the successful candidate will typically:  

* Lead complex technical projects with the potential and willingness to develop into a leading national authority in power systems testing and calibration.
* Provide specialist technical advice within their field of expertise.
* Supervise and develop staff, including mentoring early-career scientists.
* Contribute to strategic planning and future capability development.
* Build effective relationships with stakeholders and clients to achieve program outcomes.

*S&T8*  
  
At the S&T8 level, the successful candidate will in addition:  

* Provide strategic leadership for Australia's high-voltage and high-current measurement capability.
* Lead a team and allocate resources to achieve organisational objectives and national priorities.
* Influence technical directions, measurement strategies and standards development at a national and international level.
* Develop and implement long-term capability roadmaps and investment priorities.
* Act as a recognised national authority on power systems testing and calibration.
* Represent NMI in senior national and international forums and partnerships.

**Eligibility**
---------------

To be eligible for employment in the APS and the department, candidates must be Australian Citizens.  
  
Positions require a Baseline security clearance and successful candidates will be required to obtain and maintain a clearance at this level.

**Notes**
---------

A merit pool may be established and used to fill future vacancies within 18 months from the date the vacancy was first advertised in the Gazette.  
  
The department does currently offer flexible work opportunities for many roles. This position is based at NMI’s Lindfield headquarters in New South Wales, although flexible or remote work arrangements may be considered. Please reach out to the contact officer to discuss this further.

**Application information**
---------------------------

Your application must not contain any classified or sensitive information. This includes in your application responses, CV and any other documents. The selection panel may not consider applications containing classified information.  
  
Please provide a pitch explaining how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role and why you are the best candidate for the position. Your pitch can contain no more than 1000 words and should align to the key duties listed above.  
  
You may use AI tools to support your application. However, all content must be accurate, authentic, and reflect your own capability in line with APS merit principles. For further guidance, please refer to the APSC’s Principles for candidate use of AI in recruitment.  
  
Please complete your application online and provide your current CV with your application. (CVs must be in .doc, .docx, or .pdf format).  
  
Accessible application documentation is available in other formats on request. Please contact recruitment@industry.gov.au or (02) 6276 1235 if you require assistance with your application.  
  
Please refer to our Applying for a position information for additional information on how to apply.

**What’s the role?**  
You’ll help shape how people across the Data and AI Practice build their skills, understand where they are today and see what their next step could be. As Craft Pathways Product Owner, you’ll own the capability self-assessment, skills pathways and role toolkit, bringing together deep practitioner knowledge and thoughtful product ownership. You’ll design and maintain clear learning pathways, connect them to development opportunities, certifications and badging, and work with teams across the Practice to make sure they’re useful and easy to adopt. You’ll also help create skill pathways for the Data and AI Graduate Program and work closely with our Practice Community and Adoption Leads to bring the pathways to life.

**What do I need?**

* Experience designing learning or skills pathways that help people understand their proficiency and next development steps.
* Practitioner experience with understanding of Data, Analytics, and AI, with the ability to turn technical concepts into clear and practical pathways.
* Strong learning and analytics skills, with the ability to use insights to continually improve the experience.
* The ability to work with subject matter experts and stakeholders across different teams, influencing outcomes without relying on direct authority.
* A clear, accessible communication style and a focus on designing solutions with the people who’ll use them.

**Why join us?**

We’re obsessed with becoming our customers' #1 banking partner for life and we’re looking for people who are passionate about helping us achieve that goal. In return, we’re committed to making Westpac the best place to work in the country. Here are just a few of the ways we’re already doing that:

* Special offers on banking products and discounts from top brands, including generous employee-only mortgage rates!
* Flexible work arrangements to help you achieve a greater work/life balance, and a variety of leave options including Culture, Lifestyle and Wellbeing leave.
* Tailored learning and development opportunities to help your grow your career within the bank.
* Lots of opportunities to ‘give back’ to the Community by getting involved in our many volunteering initiatives.

**Create your future today**

To get started, simply click on the APPLY or APPLY NOW button

We’re all about creating a supportive and inclusive community. We welcome everyone – no matter your age, gender, background, or abilities. We also provide additional support to welcome our veterans, Indigenous Australians and neurodiverse community.

If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, you can find more information and contact details on our FAQs and how to contact us page , under the ‘Diversity, sustainability and flexibility’ section.

We may close this job advertisement earlier than the advertised closing date if suitable candidates are identified. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

**About the Opportunity**

Due to consistent growth across our business, we are seeking a motivated Graduate Engineer / Workshop Planner to join our high-performing team in Wollongong.

This is a pivotal role within our service department. Berendsen Fluid Power operates a well-equipped workshop and machine shop that overhauls and rebuilds hydraulic cylinders, pumps and motors, and is the base for a team of field service technicians providing breakdown and maintenance services to hydraulic equipment users throughout the Illawarra region.

Reporting directly to the Service Manager, this is an excellent opportunity for a suitably qualified graduate to learn all facets of the business and forge a genuine career pathway within this growing national company.

**The Role**

With training, mentoring and practical work experience, you will develop the skills and knowledge to undertake activities such as:

* Providing technical support to customers on hydraulic product selection, application, maintenance and repair
* Estimating and coordinating job workflow through to completion
* Preparing and presenting quotes and estimates for repair, manufacturing and project work
* Visiting customer sites to build relationships and develop business
* Verifying hydraulic cylinder repair scopes, including material selection, modifications and manufacturing processes
* Supporting the commercially sound operation of the workshop while meeting customer requirements
* Acting as first point of contact with sales, customers, suppliers and contractors

  

**Why Berendsen Fluid Power**

* Competitive salary package
* Supportive and professional work environment
* Career development opportunities
* Employee benefits program, including Fitness Passport
* Work for an industry leader
* 8 weeks paid parental leave and 1 week secondary carer leave
* An inclusive culture and access to our Women's Leadership Network
* A robust focus on safety through our “Home Safely Every Day” program
* Internal mentoring program

  

**About You**

To be considered for this role, you will have:

* A recent Mechanical Engineering degree or diploma, or relevant hands-on experience in a similar role
* An interest in hydraulics
* Effective communication, time management and organisation skills
* Sound computer literacy in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
* Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to work autonomously and within a team
* A safety-first mindset and the desire to build a long-standing career with Berendsen

  

**About Berendsen Fluid Power**

For more than 30 years, Berendsen has been a leading provider of hydraulic solutions, delivering repairs, overhauls, system design, manufacturing, field service and technical expertise for mission-critical industries.

We're backed by Questas Group, a strong, stable and future-focused organisation employing more than 1,000 people nationwide. Together, we are building a safer, smarter and more capable industrial future.

Ready to Step Into a Role With Real Impact?

**Junior Stockbroker**

Sydney NSW | Full time | $55,000 + super + OTE $250,000

**The markets don’t sleep. Neither does ambition.**

At Sharewise, we’re building a different kind of stockbroking firm: sharp, modern, and obsessed with giving everyday investors a real seat at the table. We’re looking for a few hungry, switched-on graduates to grow with us.

This isn’t a grad program where you rotate through departments and wait your turn. You’ll be on the desk from week one, sitting beside senior brokers, hearing how deals get done, and picking up the craft from people who live and breathe the ASX and US markets.

**What you’ll actually be doing**

* Picking up the phone to warm leads and turning conversations into long-term client relationships
* Sharing Sharewise’s market research and insights with prospects, and helping them understand what’s moving and why
* Learning about each prospect’s interests and getting them ready for meetings
* Following the ASX and US markets every day and building your knowledge of both

**Your path is mapped out**

No vague promises. Onboard 20 clients and $1m in funds under management within your first 5 months, complete your RG146, and you’ll step up to Investment Manager. From there you’re authorised to provide general advice, managing your own book, placing trades on client instruction and backed by Sharewise research. Your results decide how fast you get there, not how many years you’ve been in the building.

**You’re our kind of person if you**

* Hold a completed university degree, ideally in finance, commerce, economics or a related field
* Have sales or business development experience, ideally on the phones, or the natural ability and drive to pick it up fast
* Get a genuine buzz from targets, momentum and a good close
* Read the financial pages because you want to, not because you have to
* Speak with confidence and back it up with substance
* Want to earn your success and aren’t scared of putting in the hours to get it

**What Sharewise gives you**

* One-on-one mentoring from experienced Heads of Desk
* Structured training with full RG146 support, paid for and built into your week
* A chance to put your degree to work from day one, not years from now
* Access to Sharewise research and market insights
* Hands-on experience across both ASX and US markets, not just the local exchange
* A Sydney office with a team that celebrates wins loudly
* Uncapped earning potential and a career where your numbers do the talking

**Plenty of graduates want a job. We’re looking for the ones who want a career in the markets.**

The Media and Communications Coordinator plays a key role within the Knowledge Translation and Engagement Program of the ARC Centre of Excellence for Our Future Oceans, a major, federally funded seven-year research consortium spanning UNSW, UWA, UTAS, UQ and ANU and over 40 partner organisations globally.

The Media and Communications Coordinator develops, manages and implements all aspects of the Centre’s communications and engagement activities to deliver a cohesive and impactful Centre-wide communications strategy within a complex organisation. This role also works closely with researchers to translate and communicate the Centre’s research findings to a wide range of audiences across multiple channels including traditional media, online and social media.

* **Level 7 - 118k – 128k -** plus 17% Superannuation and annual leave loading
* Fixed Term – 3 years
* Full-time (35 hours per week)

* Develop and monitor the delivery of the Centre’s communications initiatives and projects to achieve operational and strategic goals as determined by the Centre’s leadership.
* Oversee the development of communications and impact plans and participate in consultative planning processes as required.
* Monitor, track and evaluate the effectiveness of the outputs and deliverables to ensure time, cost and quality metrics are in line with the Centre’s overall Knowledge Translation and Engagement Program.
* Provide a high level of proactive project communications support to Centre researchers and the leadership team.
* In collaboration with the Centre’s Graduate Director, develop and deliver in-house media and communications training to researchers within the centre to enable them to communicate their research clearly and confidently.

* Develop and manage effective communications with key stakeholders, both internal to UNSW and the Centre’s nodes located at other universities, and with key external partners.
* Develop strong working relationships with trusted journalists and editors in the Australian media landscape.
* Establish and implement the Centre’s social media strategy to reach specific target audiences on various platforms.
* Develop and produce engaging visual communications materials, including social media content, promotional collateral, presentations and digital assets, to support the Centre's communications and engagement objectives.
* Manage the Centre’s website, newsletters and other public facing channels.
* With the COO and Operations Team, draft, edit and publish the Centre’s Annual Report and other ad hoc reports, briefing notes, reports and government submissions.
* Participate in science outreach events with a variety of stakeholders including government, policymakers, community and schools.
* Align with and actively demonstrate the Code of Conduct and Values.
* Cooperate with all health & safety policies and procedures of the university and take all reasonable care to ensure that your actions or omissions do not impact on the psychosocial or physical health and safety of yourself or others.

* Relevant tertiary qualification in a field such as media, journalism or science communications with subsequent relevant experience or equivalent competence gained through any combination of education, training and experience.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a high level of attention to detail for deliverables produced.
* Demonstrated ability to translate complex scientific or technical subject matter into content for a range of audiences with varying degrees of subject matter familiarity.
* Demonstrated track record of producing written, visual and digital communication materials accessible to a range of stakeholders, including government, industry, and communities.

* Demonstrated success working effectively and collaboratively on initiatives with a range of people at different levels within an organisation.

At Leidos Australia, our work goes beyond a job title. We design, build, operate and support the systems, services and capabilities that help protect and advance the Australian way of life.

Backed by a global organisation of more than 40,000 people, our Australian team of around 2,000 has partnered with government, defence and national security customers for more than 30 years. We deliver mission-critical solutions where reliability, trust and purpose matter.

Leidos is a destination for people who want their work to have purpose, their contribution to be recognised, and their career to grow without needing to fit a single mould. **About Us**

OREZ is an Australian owned company forming part of the CFC Group of companies.

At OREZ, sustainability drives everything we do. As Australia’s industry leader, we specialise in advanced engineering, construction, and ongoing operational support for cutting-edge organic processing facilities. From in-vessel composting (IVC) tunnels to anaerobic digestion (AD) systems, our multidisciplinary in-house engineering team has the expertise and proven track record to deliver complex, bespoke projects.

Through exclusive partnerships with world-class OEMs, we integrate the latest technology into every solution, ensuring best-in-class performance for the organics waste processing sector. These collaborations keep us at the forefront of innovation, delivering unparalleled value to our clients.

We understand the unique commercial challenges each project presents. By offering flexible, tailored solutions, we align with our clients’ goals, forging strong, long-lasting partnerships. We are committed to delivering safe and capital efficient projects for our clients.

Our commitment to sustainable practices is deeply rooted in our RIPPA values: Respect, Integrity, Passion, Persistence, and Accountability.

At OREZ, we’re more than problem-solvers — we’re catalysts for change, driving the shift toward a cleaner, healthier planet.

#### **Job Description**

We are an engineering led delivery company specialising in advanced bioenergy and composting. We design, deliver and commission the facilities that turn kerbside collected FOGO and industrial food organics into energy, compost and recovered resources, working with local and state government, major corporates and private operators, and bringing proven European technology to Australian conditions through partners such as Thoni and Bianna. OREZ is part of the CFC Group, which gives us the backing of a larger organisation while keeping the pace and autonomy of a growing specialist business.

We are looking for a Project Engineer to join our team in Sutherland. You will work alongside our Project Managers and senior engineers across live projects, from early contractor involvement through design, procurement, construction and commissioning. It is broad, hands on work, and it is a deliberate development role: depending on where your strengths sit, it leads either into project management or into technical specialisation.

**What you will be doing**

* Supporting project delivery: RFIs and technical queries, programme and progress tracking, procurement and expediting, document control and reporting.
* Technical work: drawings, markups, bills of material, basic calculations, design and constructability reviews, vendor evaluation and testing.
* Getting on site: coordination, inspections, subcontractor liaison, commissioning support and handover documentation.
* Working directly with clients and vendors as a day to day contact on your packages.

**What we are looking for**

* An engineering degree, mechanical, process, electrical, civil or chemical, or equivalent.
* Up to around four years of relevant experience. Strong graduates are encouraged to apply.
* Clear communication and the confidence to deal with clients, vendors and site teams.
* Strong organisation, and the ability to run several tasks at once with limited supervision.
* Australian working rights, a driver licence, and willingness to travel interstate.

CAD, scheduling tools, Procore, a White Card, or experience in waste, water, food processing or materials handling will all be well regarded, though none are essential.

#### **Desired Skills and Experience**

**Why OREZ**

* Real exposure to complex projects end to end.
* Mentoring from experienced engineers and project managers, inside a clear career pathway with transparent role bands.
* Travel to projects around Australia, and the potential to visit our technology partners in Europe.
* Participation in the Annual Incentive Plan, plus Employee Assistance Program access and a flexible, practical working culture.
* A small, capable team where what you do is visible and matters.

If this sounds like the next step for you, apply with your CV and a short cover letter telling us what interests you about the work. We review applications as they arrive.
